stem: Which of the following best describes a reasonable target for a deliberate forgetting policy?

options.text: Only information that was created on a Tuesday
Every single piece of information regardless of whether it's still useful
Information that has been explicitly superseded or has become reliably irrelevant
Nothing should ever be targeted for forgetting under any policy

explanation.why_correct: A reasonable forgetting policy targets information that's been explicitly superseded (like an old address replaced by a new one) or has become reliably irrelevant, rather than discarding indiscriminately.

why_incorrect.B: Discarding everything regardless of usefulness is indiscriminate forgetting, which risks losing genuinely valuable information.
why_incorrect.D: Some deliberate forgetting of clearly outdated or superseded information is actually beneficial, as discussed.
why_incorrect.A: Day of creation has no principled relationship to whether information is actually outdated or irrelevant.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Target deliberate forgetting at explicitly superseded or reliably irrelevant information, not at everything indiscriminately or based on arbitrary criteria.

stem: One memory retriever uses exact keyword matching and misses a relevant note that is worded differently, while a second pipeline packs 40 retrieved notes into a single prompt. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: If a memory appears anywhere in the prompt, the model is guaranteed to use it
Literal keyword matching can miss relevant memories phrased differently, so similarity-based relevance is often preferable
Adding more retrieved items never hurts because each one adds helpful context
A missed match proves the note was never stored
Items buried in the middle of a long memory block can be overlooked, so fewer, better items with the strongest at the edges help

explanation.why_correct: Exact matching depends on shared wording, so a similarity-based measure surfaces relevant notes that use different words. Separately, being present in the prompt is not the same as being used: models attend less reliably to the middle of long contexts, so retrieving fewer, higher-quality items and placing the best at the edges is a cheap mitigation.

why_incorrect.A: Long-context models can overlook information in poorly attended positions even when it is present.
why_incorrect.C: Extra items add distractors and push relevant ones toward the weakly used middle, so returns diminish and can turn negative.
why_incorrect.D: The note can exist yet not be surfaced; the failure here is the matching method, not storage.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Retrieve with a real relevance measure, keep the set small, and put the strongest items at the edges -- in the prompt is not the same as used.

stem: A memory store retains an old, now-superseded fact alongside the new, correct one, with no indication of which is current, and the retrieval system ranks purely by topical relevance with no recency weighting. What is the likely consequence?

options.text: The system might surface the outdated fact as if it were still current, since relevance alone doesn't distinguish which version is more recent or accurate now
The system will always automatically prefer the correct, current fact with no further design needed
This combination guarantees perfectly accurate retrieval in every case
This has no bearing on retrieval accuracy whatsoever

explanation.why_correct: Without recency weighting or a forgetting mechanism to deprioritize the superseded fact, a purely relevance-based ranking has no way to distinguish the outdated version from the current one, risking the outdated fact being surfaced as if it were still accurate.

why_incorrect.B: Without recency as a signal (or forgetting to remove the stale version), there's no mechanism ensuring the correct, current fact is preferred over the outdated one.
why_incorrect.C: This combination of retaining stale facts and ranking by relevance alone is precisely the scenario that risks inaccurate retrieval, not guaranteed accuracy.
why_incorrect.D: This combination has a direct, meaningful negative bearing on retrieval accuracy, as described.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Retaining superseded facts without recency weighting or forgetting risks outdated information being surfaced as if it were still current.
